title: His first drum sets: pony set and gold sparkle kit
summary: His first set was a Wurlitzer pony set bought in Kansas City; in Omaha he bought a gold sparkle set that was shipped to Ottumwa.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Isn't that funny? Listen, Gus, you didn't tell me, you must have bought your drums by now.
Yes, I bought -- I had a set of drums when I went to Omaha, Nebraska. I bought a new set in Omaha.
So, after you heard Jo Jones and everything. Did you own drums then?
Oh, yes.
Oh, you did.
Yes, yes, I --
In other words, when you came to Kansas
City, you got yourself some drums.
Yes, when I came to Kansas City, I bought myself a set of drums.
Yeah.
And my first drum set was from Wurlitzer. It was called the a pony set, see. And really, I loved that little old set.
Oh, that must have been a big thrill to you, wasn't it?
Well, sure, and I hated to turn it in on the new set that I bought in Omaha, Nebraska. I bought a gold sparkling set in Omaha, when I left there. So when I got to Ottumwa, --
Yeah.
Well, they sent the drums from Omaha to me, see.
Oh, they did.
Yeah.
Shipped them to you, huh?
Shipped them to me.
They were pleased to have you playing their drums.
I had to pay for them.
Oh, you paid for them.
I paid for them in Omaha, yes.
Oh, yes.
Sure.
Yeah, yeah.
And I was happy, though, because they were sparkling and everything.
Sure, yeah.
